title: UUID Generation
description: UUIDs (Universally Unique Identifiers) are 128-bit identifiers used to uniquely identify information. Version 4 UUIDs are randomly generated and have a format like 'xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx'. They're commonly used for database primary keys, session IDs, and distributed systems. The UUID module from the standard library provides UUID generation and parsing. This example demonstrates how to use it.
code: printf("  Random UUID is nil: %s\n", uuid1.isNil() ? "true" : "false");
printf("  Nil UUID is nil: %s\n", uuid2.isNil() ? "true" : "false");
